skill.description: Browser automation using Playwright MCP for navigation, form interaction, screenshots, snapshots, data extraction, and controlled browser workflows.
skill.summary: Automate browser navigation, forms, screenshots, and data checks through Playwright MCP.
skill.author: 92Bilal26

security_audit.summary: Most documentation findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, JSON Schema URLs, or localhost examples. Real risks remain in shell-based stdio command execution, predictable /tmp PID files, unpinned npx @latest execution, browser code execution, and local file upload capability. No prompt injection or hidden malicious intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.suggestion: Pin @playwright/mcp to a reviewed version and update it through a documented release process.

remediation.issue: Stdio transport executes a caller-supplied command through the shell
remediation.suggestion: Avoid shell=True, parse commands into argv arrays, and allow only documented MCP server commands.

remediation.issue: Predictable PID files in /tmp control server shutdown behavior
remediation.suggestion: Use a user-owned runtime directory, validate numeric PIDs, and avoid broad pkill patterns.

remediation.issue: Browser code execution and file upload can expose sensitive session or local data
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before browser_run_code, browser_evaluate, form submission, or file upload actions.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Runtime Package Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill instructs and the helper script runs npx @playwright/mcp@latest. This executes whatever package version is latest at runtime, which can bypass marketplace review and reproducibility.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both the documentation and startup script explicitly use @latest. Running an unpinned package at install or task time is a clear supply-chain risk.

semantic_findings.title: Browser Code Execution Capability
semantic_findings.description: The documented browser_run_code tool accepts a JavaScript Playwright function for the active browser page. Misuse can manipulate logged-in pages or extract page data from a shared browser context.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The tool documentation and skill example both show arbitrary Playwright code supplied as a parameter. The capability is intentional but security-sensitive.

semantic_findings.title: Local File Upload Capability
semantic_findings.description: The referenced browser_file_upload tool accepts absolute local paths for upload. If an agent follows untrusted page instructions, this can expose sensitive local files to a website.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The tool schema explicitly describes absolute paths for upload. There is no evidence of malicious intent, but the data-exfiltration capability is real.

content.user_title: Automate Browser Tasks with Playwright MCP
content.value_statement: Browser tasks often require repeated navigation, form filling, and page checks. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a Playwright MCP workflow for controlled browser automation.
actual_capabilities: Starts and stops a local Playwright MCP server with helper scripts.
Navigates pages, goes back, opens tabs, and waits for page conditions.
Captures screenshots and accessibility snapshots for page inspection.
Clicks elements, types text, fills forms, selects options, and handles dialogs.
Runs approved browser evaluation or Playwright snippets for complex workflows.
Lists and calls MCP tools through HTTP or stdio transports.
limitations: Requires Node, npx, Python 3, and Playwright MCP availability.
Live websites may block automation, require login, or change without notice.
Shared browser state can persist between calls until the server is stopped.
Stdio command mode should be used only with trusted local commands.

use_cases.title: Check Web UI Flows
use_cases.description: Run repeatable browser steps, capture snapshots, and report broken states before release.

use_cases.title: Collect Public Web Data
use_cases.description: Navigate public pages, extract visible facts, and return concise findings with page context.

use_cases.title: Automate Admin Tasks
use_cases.description: Use approved browser actions to complete repetitive forms or dashboard checks.

prompt_templates.title: Open a Page and Snapshot
prompt_templates.prompt: Start the browser MCP server, navigate to the target URL, capture an accessibility snapshot, and summarize the visible controls.

prompt_templates.title: Fill a Form Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the page snapshot to find form fields, fill only the approved values, submit the form, and report the confirmation text.

prompt_templates.title: Test a User Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the requested checkout or signup flow, capture screenshots at key states, and list any failed steps.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Structured Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Navigate through the requested pages, use browser evaluation only after approval, extract the required facts, and include source page titles.

output_examples.input: Verify whether the pricing page has a contact sales call to action.
output_examples.output: The report names the page visited, the visible call to action, and a screenshot filename for review.

output_examples.input: Fill a demo request form with approved test contact details.
output_examples.output: The result confirms the fields used, the submit action, and the confirmation message shown by the site.

output_examples.input: Collect product names from a catalog page.
output_examples.output: A concise list of product names with the page title and any pagination notes.

best_practices: Capture a snapshot before clicking or typing so actions target current element references.
Use trusted local MCP endpoints and close the browser when work is complete.
Confirm approval before uploading files, submitting forms, or running browser code.
anti_patterns: Do not run stdio commands from untrusted prompts or copied web content.
Do not upload local files unless the user named the exact files and destination.
Do not automate account changes or purchases without explicit approval.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It automates browser navigation, snapshots, screenshots, forms, clicks, waits, and approved Playwright actions.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require a browser server?
faq.answer: Yes. It starts a local Playwright MCP server before browser tools can be called.

faq.question: Can it interact with logged-in sessions?
faq.answer: Yes. The shared browser context can keep session state until the server is stopped.

faq.question: Can it upload files?
faq.answer: The referenced Playwright tool supports file upload, so users should approve exact paths first.

faq.question: Is it safe for untrusted websites?
faq.answer: Use caution. Untrusted pages can influence visible content and should not authorize sensitive actions.
